overview: In From's Gambit move order Black replies 2...Ne7 instead of 2...d6, planning ...Ng6 to regain the pawn on e5. White can protect e5 with Nf3 or d4 and hold the extra pawn. I am unsure of the details; the position is a rare Black gambit side line.

white_ideas.idea: Keep the pawn with Nf3 and d4
Develop and use the open f-file

black_ideas.idea: Play ...d6 and open lines for the pieces

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White e5 pawn and Black f-pawn gone

character.notes: An unusual gambit with open lines and early tactics.

gambit.notes: Black offers the e5 pawn which White can hold by Nf3.

soundness.notes: Considered inferior to the main From's Gambit.

sublines_that_differ.name: From's Gambit 2...d6
sublines_that_differ.how: Normal From's with more tactical play.

character.reason: Early gambit play with open lines and weak king positions.

gambit.reason: Black offers the e-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: Slow compensation compared with the main From line.

structure.reason: Central pawns come off, leaving open lines.

approach.reason: Strong players do not play it.

plans.reason: Black sacrifices the pawn for faster development.
